issues.problem: The dossier presents destruction of the only described verifiable attendance records as a normal continuing protocol for a EUR 296,400 CERV project, before its August 2026 final technical report. CERV grant terms require retained evidence of implementation and generally five years after final payment at this grant size. No alternative auditable participation evidence is described. This is an unintended realism defect, not a reason to resolve the deliberately disputed 84/96 unique-resident total or to add an outside-law trap.
issues.fix: Preserve the March destruction and I1 exactly as unresolved historical facts, but identify the destruction as a documented error. Replace the continuing rule with a dated 30 September 2026 corrective addendum: 'Future grant-relevant attendance evidence will be securely retained for five years after final payment, or longer while an audit or proceeding remains open; unnecessary copies will be deleted. The 2025 source sheets and participant identifiers were prematurely destroyed on 31 March 2026 and cannot be recovered; this incident has been recorded and notified to the grant authority. The aggregate annual-report and consolidation totals remain unreconciled.' Update F21 to distinguish the old error from the new policy. Do not introduce a surviving person-level 2025 register or a reconciled count.
